# aslnut

> aslnut is a TypeScript library that makes and runs worlds in the browser on WebGPU and WebGL2: the Earth (or a flat floor) with imagery and terrain, your data drawn as layers, roads, buildings and trees, moving fleets, and things of your own (levels, moving parts, copies over time, clones that each look different). This file is everything an assistant needs to write one: the authoring guide, six complete recipes, every import, and an index of every part that exists.

Generated by docs/_tree/llms.mjs from docs/authoring.md, examples/recipes, the package's entry files, docs/reference and the tree (docs/_tree/spec.txt). Do not edit it: edit those.

## The authoring guide

**In one line:** aslnut makes **worlds** in the browser on WebGPU and WebGL2: the Earth (or a flat floor), what stands on it, what moves on it, and your data drawn over it. This page is enough to write one. The [recipes](#recipes) are six complete scripts, one per kind of app; [llms.txt](#api-index) carries this page, the recipes, every import and every part's signature (generated: it never drifts). Wrapping aslnut into a platform of your own (components, a flow runtime, a server): the [implementers' guide](implementers.md).

```ts
import { data, earth, imagery, layer, legend, scale, terrain, world } from 'aslnut';

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const w = await world(canvas, {                                              // a promise: await it
  body: earth({ imagery: [imagery.esri()], terrain: [terrain.mapzen()] }),   // the ground: lists of providers
  view: { lon: 145.12, lat: -37.92, zoom: 14, tilt: 40, bearing: 0 },        // where the camera starts
});
w.add(layer({                                                                // one dataset said one way
  id: 'suburbs', label: 'Suburbs by rate', data: data.geojson('suburbs.geojson'),   // loaded once
  area: { color: scale.quantile((d) => Number(d.props.rate), { range: 'reds' }), opacity: 0.8 }, // classes from all of it
  labels: { text: (d) => String(d.props.name) },                            // its names, inside the layer
  tooltip: (d) => `${d.props.name}: ${d.props.rate}`,
}));
legend(w, { for: 'suburbs', title: 'Rate' });
await w.settled();                                                           // the view complete: tiles, data, builds
```

## The model

- **A world stands on a body:** `earth({ imagery, terrain, sky })`, or `plane()` for a flat floor. A view is `{ lon, lat, zoom, tilt, bearing }` (degrees; tilt 0 looks straight down). The view now is `w.camera.view`, in the same terms: `w.fly({ ...w.camera.view, tilt: 40 })`.
- **Elements are added and named:** `w.add(a, b, …)`. Each has an `id`: `w.element(id).setProps({ … })`, `w.hide(id)`, `w.reveal(id)`, `w.remove(id)`; `w.list` is every element, and `w.on('elements', …)` hears the list change.
- **A layer is a statement:** one dataset said one way. `layer({ id, data, area, line, points, extrusion, labels, legend })` holds its data (loaded once, shared by its signs), its signs, its names (`labels`) and its legend: one switch, one place in the stack. A mark alone (`points`, `line`, `area`, `extrusion`, `text`, `raster`, `arc`, `trail`) is a layer of one sign.
- **Data becomes signs:** a source (`data.geojson`, `data.csv`, `data.wfs`, `data.pmtiles`, `data.rows`, `data.query`) feeds a layer. A style prop takes a value, your function of the feature `(d) => …` (its fields in `d.props`), or a `scale.*`. A scale's classes come from the whole data: the same value gives the same look at every zoom. Rows join shapes by a key: `districts.join(rows, { on: 'code' })` (two sources, one of shapes).
- **orbit › observation › data › viz:** the camera only moves the picture. A GIS view has no levels: every layer is shown and stays. A twin is looked at through levels (`world(…, { observation: { levels: 'default' } })`: world › country › region › city › district › street › building › room), and `when: { level: { from: 'district' } }` decides what is present. A level changes past a margin and after a dwell; `w.setLevel('street')` sets it; `w.on('level', …)` hears it.
- **Things stand and move:** ready-made elements from data (`roads`, `buildings`, `vegetation`, `water`); your own shapes (`shape({ params, build })`) placed by `entities({ shape, data })`; moving sets from a log (`entities({ shape, drive: drive.data(log) })`).
- **Kinds and traits:** a kind (`kinds.house`, `office`, `charger`, `vehicle`, or yours: `kind({ name, traits })`) names what every design of it carries: anchors (`entry`, `parking`, `service`), measures (its footprint, its front at +z, its roof), params (`levels`). `shape({ kind, build })` places them with `b.anchor(…)`; `shape.check({ kind })` says what is missing or misplaced; `traits(made, kind)` reads them.
- **`when` decides showing,** on every element and provider: `true`, `{ level }`, or `(s) => …` of the state (`s.observation.level`, `s.time`, `s.user.toggles`, `s.world.params`). Never of the camera.
- **Knobs and queries:** `w.param('group.name', spec, set)` declares a knob, `w.set(key, value)` turns it; a `data.query` with `deps` asks again and its layers recolour.
- **The camera:** `w.go(view)` and `w.fly(view)` set it; `w.follow(thing)` keeps it on a moving thing on damped springs (`track(log, id)`, a point, your function of the time; `heading: true` turns with it); `w.play(moves.chase(thing, { behind, up }))` plays a move (chase, track, crane, dolly, arc, reveal, or `move({ aim: lookAt(thing), keys })` of your own: rigs round what it looks at, each key's ease), a thing in the air looked at where it is. A view tilts to 88° with the eye at street level, 80° high up; the eye stays over the ground.
- **Recording:** `for await (const f of w.record({ fps: 30, seconds: 8, path }))` steps the world's clock a frame at a time, holds each frame until it is complete and reads it back: the same frames on every run. Your code that sets the camera each frame goes in `w.everyFrame(fn, { before: true })`.
- **Settled and report:** `await w.settled()` waits until the view is complete; `w.report()` says what is pending or failed.

## Your own thing

A thing is one `shape`. Its build says what it is (the builder's verbs), what can move (a part's joint), where things attach (anchors) and what repeats over time (`emit`). The element that places it gives the drivers, the attachments and each clone's look.

```ts
// (tri: a triangle's three points; data: your points; walls, roofs: your colours)
const thing = shape({
  id: 'mill', params: { width: num(6, 12, 8) },                 // params: what changes its geometry (one build each, cached)
  build: (b, p) => {                                            // metres in its frame: its foot at y 0, its front +z
    b.solid('box', { size: [p.width, 5, 7], at: [0, 2.5, 0], tint: true });          // takes each clone's colour
    b.group('roof', (b) => b.solid('box', { size: [p.width, 1, 7], at: [0, 5.5, 0] })); // a group: a colour per clone
    b.part('wheel', (b) => b.solid('cylinder', { radius: 2, size: .3, axis: 'x', at: [5, 2, 0] }),
      { pivot: [5, 2, 0], joint: { kind: 'hinge', axis: 'x' } });                  // can turn; nothing turns it yet
    b.anchor('chimney', [1, 9, -2], { kind: 'stack' });                            // where things attach
    b.frame({ at: [1, 9, -2] }, (b) => b.copy((b) => b.mesh(tri), { emit: { count: [24, 8, 0], life: 4, rise: 12, fade: [.7, 0] } }));
  },
  simple: true,                                                 // level 1: the same build, fewer sides
  far: (b, p) => b.solid('box', { size: [p.width, 7, 7], at: [0, 3.5, 0], tint: true }), // level 2: your symbol
  size: { min: 4 },                                             // never under 4 CSS px across
});
const set = entities({ id: 'mills', shape: thing, data,
  variation: { seed: (d) => String(d.id), color: .06, scale: .1 },  // a seeded spread round each colour and size
  tint: (d) => walls[Number(d.props.n) % 4]!, tints: { roof: (d) => roofs[Number(d.props.n) % 3] },
  heading: (d) => Number(d.props.facing), stretch: (d) => 1 + Number(d.props.n) % 3 * .1, // taller (parts ride along)
  joints: { wheel: (d) => ({ rate: Number(d.props.rpm), unit: 'rpm' }) },  // turned on the chip from the clock
  pixels: { full: 120, simple: 25, margin: .2 } });                // each clone's level by its size on screen
w.add(set);
set.joint('m7', 'wheel', { rate: 0 });                             // one clone changed in one write
```

| brick | how | what to know |
|---|---|---|
| levels | `simple: true \| (b, p) => …` · `far: (b, p) => … \| 'box' \| 'dot' \| 'impostor'` · `detail: 0 \| 1 \| 2` on any verb | each clone takes its level by the pixels it covers (`pixels: { full, simple, margin }`); the margin stops it flipping at an edge; unset levels cost nothing (the whole stands in) |
| parts that move | `b.part(name, fn, { pivot, joint: { kind: 'hinge' \| 'wheel' \| 'slider', axis } })` | the element drives it: `joints: { name: { rate, unit } }`, each clone's own `(d) => …`, a formula (`{ formula: 'value = 30.0 * sin(time * 0.5 + seed * 6.28);' }`, degrees), or a log's value (`{ value: 'travel' }` with `history.log({ travel: true })`: every wheel rolls by its car's travel) |
| copies over time | `b.copy(fn, { emit: { count: [whole, simple, far], life, rise, spread, grow, fade, drift } })` | smoke, steam, sparks: born again every `life` seconds, moved and faded on the chip; two a shape, up to 1,023 copies each |
| anchors and attach | `b.anchor(name, at, { kind })` · `entities({ attach: [{ shape: smoke, at: 'stack' }] })` | a shape at every anchor of that name or kind of every clone (still things; on moving ones planned) |
| bodies from a profile | `b.mesh(triangles, { smooth: true, crease: 50 })` · `shape({ defaults: (given) => row })` | your own loft (sections station by station) drawn as smooth panels, edges past the crease kept sharp; a type given brings its row of numbers, what is given besides stands over it |
| vehicles | `cars.make({ type: 'suv' })` · `cars.suv` · `entities({ shape: cars.shape, params: (d) => ({ type: d.props.kind }) })` | each type one row of its silhouette (`presets.json`: wheelbase, overhangs, bonnet, rake, roofline, tail and its rake, clearance, wheel, arch, belt, glass, windows, cladding, lights, load): a new body is a row, not code; `tints: { glass, cladding, load }`; a tractor's trailer turns at its fifth wheel by its track: `log.appendMany(cars.hitch(rows, tractor))` with `joints: { trailer: { value: 'hitch' } }` |
| clones with variety | `tint`, `tints: { group }` (four groups), `stretch`, `scale`, `heading`, `variation: { seed, color, scale, builds }` | a clone is a record on the chip, no geometry of its own: vary the record, build only what changes the geometry (each distinct params × builds is one more draw) |
| size | marks: `size: { m: 40, min: 4, max: 32 }` (metres kept within CSS px) or `{ px: 8 }` · a shape: `size: { min, max }` (px) | one rule for points, lines, arcs, text and shapes: zoom writes nothing |
| priorities | `w.setPriorities({ drop: ['parked'], keep: ['cars'] })` | on a slow device, what loses detail first and what never does |

## React

`aslnut/react` is the same API in a React app (React 18 or 19, an optional peer). `<World>` makes the world on mount and disposes it on unmount; its `elements` are aslnut's own objects, made in render:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { layer, plane, scale, type Feature, type Picked } from 'aslnut';
import { World, useWorldEvent } from 'aslnut/react';

const BODY = plane();                                                       // made once, outside the component
const BY_KIND = scale.category((d: Feature) => String(d.props.kind), { range: 'set2' });
const BY_RATE = scale.quantile((d: Feature) => Number(d.props.rate), { range: 'blues' });

function Map({ blocks }: { blocks: Feature[] }) {
  const [byRate, setByRate] = useState(false);
  return (
    <World options={{ body: BODY, view: { lon: 0, lat: 0, zoom: 16 } }} style={{ height: '100dvh' }}
      elements={[layer({ id: 'blocks', data: blocks, area: { color: byRate ? BY_RATE : BY_KIND } })]}  // a change: setProps
      onReady={(w) => console.log(w.api)}>
      <button onClick={() => setByRate((x) => !x)}>colour</button>
      <Panel />
    </World>
  );
}
function Panel() {                                                           // inside <World>: the hooks
  const [picked, setPicked] = useState<Picked | null>(null);
  useWorldEvent('tap', (p) => setPicked(p));
  return picked && <aside>{String(picked.props.name)}</aside>;
}
```

- **Elements are matched by `id`** from one render to the next: a new id is added, a gone one removed, a changed prop set on the element already in the world (`setProps`: a restyle, never a rebuild). Give every element an `id`.
- **Make sources, logs, scales and functions once** (outside the component or with `useMemo`): one made again in render is a new prop each render (a restyle, or for a source a load). Plain values and objects are compared by value.
- **`options`** are what the world is made with. Later, `views`, `time`, `timeZone`, `quality`, `render.shadows`, `theme`, `budget`, `priorities` and `observation` follow their changes; the rest stay (a new world: a new `key`). A changed `view` moves the camera only with `viewChange="go"` or `viewChange={{ seconds: 1.5 }}`.
- **Hooks:** `useWorld()` (null until ready), `useElement(id)`, `useWorldEvent(name, fn)`. The world in `onReady` is the plain one: `w.fly`, `replay(w, …)`, `w.on`.
- **Give `<World>` a size** (`style` or a class); the canvas fills it, the children are drawn over it. On a server it renders an empty box.

## The rules

1. **Pay only for what you set.** Every option is optional, and an unset one costs nothing. Start with a few props.
2. **Everything is configurable** through provider factories with defaults: `imagery.esri({ layer: 'light' })`, `imagery.osm()`, `imagery.custom({ url })`; `terrain.mapzen()`, `terrain.custom({ heights })`; `terrain: []` is flat. Any value can be your function.
3. **WebGPU and WebGL2, both.** `world()` picks one (`graphics: 'auto'`). The API and the picture are the same on both: never write for one only.
4. **One import:** everything comes from `'aslnut'`, except the ready-made people, vehicles and drones: `'aslnut/modules/presets/humans'`, `'…/vehicles'` (`cars`), `'…/drones'`; and the React shell: `'aslnut/react'`.
5. **Errors say the fix:** an `AslnutError` has a `code`, a `message` and a `fix`.

## Pick a recipe

| app | recipe | what it uses |
|---|---|---|
| GIS view | `gis-view` | `imagery.esri({ layer: 'light' })`, `raster.wms`, `data.wfs(url, { typeName, extent })`, `layer({ area, labels })`, `area` / `line` / `points`, `layers(w)`, `legend(w)` |
| district twin | `district-twin` | `roads`, `buildings`, `vegetation`, `sky()`, `render: { shadows: true }`, `time`, `observation: { levels }`, `when: { level }` |
| fleet | `fleet` | `history.log({ values, travel })` + `appendMany`, `entities({ drive: drive.data(log), joints, trail, gauge })`, `replay` |
| analysis view | `analysis` | `theme.dark()`, `subject: true`, `layer` with `scale.quantile` and `labels`, `legend`, `tooltip`, `w.param` + `data.query` + `join` |
| your design of a kind | `own-kind` | `shape({ kind, build })`, `b.group('walls')`, `b.anchor`, `shape.check({ kind })`, `shapes.import(url, { kind, anchors })`, `entities` |
| your own thing | `own-thing` | `shape({ build, simple, far, size })`, `b.part` with a joint, `b.copy` with `emit`, `entities({ variation, tint, tints, joints, pixels })`, `set.joint` |

## Common mistakes

- `d.props.x` is `unknown`: write `String(d.props.name)` or `Number(d.props.rate)` where a string or a number is wanted.
- `earth()` takes lists: `imagery: [imagery.esri()]`, `terrain: [terrain.mapzen()]`.
- A feature you write in code has `props`, not `properties`: `{ id: 'a', props: {}, geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [lon, lat] } }`.
- Names as a second element of the same data: put them in the layer (`layer({ data, area, labels: { text } })`).
- A zoom range or a colour that reads the camera: a GIS layer needs no gate, and a look comes from the data only. In a twin, gate presence by level (`when: { level }`) with `observation: { levels: 'default' }` on the world; `when: { zoom }` does not exist.
- A WMS is a picture: `raster({ source: raster.wms(url, { layers }) })`. A WFS is data, loaded once: `data.wfs(url, { typeName, extent })` (give the `extent` unless the layer is small). A tiled source (`data.pmtiles`, `data.wfs(…, { tiles: true })`) needs its scale's `domain`.
- `legend(w, { for: id })` needs that layer's `color` to be a `scale.*`. `layers(w)` lists the elements that have a `label`.
- A theme mutes everything that is not a subject: give your data layers `subject: true`.
- `w.set(key, v)` needs the knob declared first: `w.param('stats.year', { type: 'number', range: [2019, 2025], default: 2025 }, () => {})`. Keys are dotted.
- Moving things need the clock to run: `replay(w, { log, play: true })`. A gauge shows only where the shape is drawn unless you give it `within` (metres).
- Shadows need a sun: `earth({ sky: sky() })` with `world(…, { render: { shadows: true }, time })` at a daytime hour.
- A part does not move by itself: give its driver in the element's `joints`. A wheel looks the same at every angle: give it spokes or paddles to show it turning.
- `b.mesh` takes its triangles as listed: each faces the side from which its three points run counter-clockwise (that side is lit). The solids and sweeps face outward by themselves.
- A small thing at street zoom (a 2 m cart covers a few px at zoom 17): give its shape the size rule's floor, `size: { min: 8 }` (CSS px), so it stays readable, and expect its whole level only close up (`pixels: { full, simple }` say when).
- Each distinct `params` is a build of its own (and a draw a chunk a level): vary what only looks different with `tint`, `tints`, `stretch`, `scale` and `heading`, not params.
- Anchors are in the shape's frame (metres, its foot at y 0, its front +z) and must meet the kind's traits (llms.txt › Kinds): a house wants an `entry` at the front on the ground, `parking` outside the walls and a `service` point on the ground; an office two entries and four parking bays. An anchor marks where a thing goes: draw the building only, and place what stands at an anchor (a charger, a car) as its own entity. The footprint is the box of a group named `'walls'` when the shape has one (`b.group('walls', …)`), else of all that stands over 0.3 m: without it, a post or a letterbox out by the drive puts the bays inside it.
- `shape.check({ kind })` builds the shape at every param's ends (each min and max): the traits must hold at all of them, so make the counts hold at the smallest size too (enough bays on the narrowest office).
- A model from `shapes.import(url, …)` is placed as it is: `entities({ shape: model, data })`.
- A camera set each frame in `w.on('frame', …)` or a plain `w.everyFrame` lands on the next frame (they run after the draws): use `w.everyFrame(fn, { before: true })`, or a move (`w.play`). A follow need not be asked again each frame: a zoom goes on following, only a pan ends it.
- Never invent a prop or a function: look it up in the API index. A part marked planned does not exist yet.

## Recipes

Each one is a complete script for a page with a <canvas>; checked on WebGPU and WebGL2 (tools/smoke-recipes.mjs).

### gis-view

A GIS view: Esri's light grey map on the terrain, a WMS picture (planning zones) and WFS features of every geometry type (polygons, multipolygons, lines, multilines, multipoints, points) from a public map and feature service, each loaded once over the area and each with a tooltip; the suburbs and their names as one layer; the layer list (show, fade, drag to reorder, each layer's legend) and a legend box. No levels and no gates: the camera only moves the picture.

```ts
import { area, data, earth, imagery, layer, layers, legend, line, points, raster, scale, terrain, world } from 'aslnut';

// a public GeoServer (WMS and WFS; it lets any site read it, so no proxy is needed)
const OWS = 'https://opendata.maps.vic.gov.au/geoserver';
const NS = 'open-data-platform';
const credit = '© State of Victoria (DEECA), CC BY 4.0';
// the area every WFS layer is loaded over, once: [west, south, east, north] in degrees
const AREA: [number, number, number, number] = [145.07, -37.96, 145.18, -37.89];
const wfs = (name: string) => data.wfs(`${OWS}/wfs`, { typeName: `${NS}:${name}`, extent: AREA, attribution: credit });

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const w = await world(canvas, {
  body: earth({ imagery: [imagery.esri({ layer: 'light' })], terrain: [terrain.mapzen()] }),
  view: { lon: 145.1215, lat: -37.9235, zoom: 15.6, tilt: 30, bearing: 0 },
});

const KINDS = ['education centre', 'hospital', 'community venue', 'emergency facility', 'recreational resource'];
w.add(
  // a WMS layer as one picture of the view, stacked with the vectors
  raster({ id: 'zones', label: 'Planning zones (WMS)', source: raster.wms(`${OWS}/wms`, { layers: `${NS}:plan_zone`, single: true, attribution: credit }), opacity: 0.45 }),
  // one statement: the suburbs (polygons) with their names inside the same layer (one switch, one place in the stack)
  layer({ id: 'suburbs', label: 'Suburbs (polygons)', data: wfs('vmlite_locality_polygon'),
    area: { color: '#93c5fd', opacity: 0.25, outline: { color: '#ffffff', width: 1 } },
    labels: { text: (d) => String(d.props.locality_name), size: 13, color: '#1f2937', halo: { width: 3, color: '#ffffff' } },
    tooltip: (d) => String(d.props.locality_name), hover: { color: '#ffffff', mix: 0.3 } }),
  // a mark alone is a layer of one sign
  area({ id: 'sites', label: 'Sites (multipolygons)', data: wfs('foi_polygon'), color: scale.category((d) => String(d.props.feature_type), { range: 'set2' }),
    opacity: 0.6, outline: { color: '#334155', width: 0.8 }, tooltip: (d) => `${d.props.name}\n${d.props.feature_type}` }),
  line({ id: 'creeks', label: 'Creeks (lines)', data: wfs('hy_watercourse'), width: 2.2, color: '#2563eb', tooltip: (d) => String(d.props.name ?? 'creek') }),
  line({ id: 'pipelines', label: 'Pipelines (multilines)', data: wfs('foi_line'), width: 2.4, color: '#ea580c', dashes: [10, 6], tooltip: (d) => String(d.props.name) }),
  points({ id: 'places', label: 'Places (multipoints)', data: wfs('foi_point'), size: 9, outline: { color: '#ffffff', width: 1.5 },
    color: scale.category((d) => String(d.props.feature_type), { domain: KINDS, range: ['#f97316', '#ef4444', '#8b5cf6', '#dc2626', '#16a34a'] }), tooltip: (d) => String(d.props.name) }),
  points({ id: 'dams', label: 'Dams (points)', data: wfs('hy_water_point'), size: 11, color: '#0284c7', outline: { color: '#ffffff', width: 2 }, tooltip: (d) => String(d.props.name) }),
);

// the layer list: every layer with a label (show, fade, drag to reorder; a WMS layer's own legend picture)
layers(w, { title: 'Layers' });
// a legend box for one layer's colour scale
legend(w, { for: 'places', title: 'Places by kind' });
```

### district-twin

A district twin: satellite imagery on the terrain, the streets built from their centre lines and tags, buildings raised from their footprints (houses with pitched roofs, offices with windows), street trees grown from their species, all lit by the real sun for the place and time, with shadows. A twin is looked at through levels: the buildings and trees are present from the district level in (a level changes past a margin and after a dwell, never with each move of the camera). Your data: three GeoJSON files.

```ts
import { buildings, data, earth, imagery, roads, sky, terrain, vegetation, world, zonedTime } from 'aslnut';

// your district's data (an OpenStreetMap or Overture extract works as it is)
const ROADS = 'data/roads.geojson';         // centre lines with OSM tags: highway, lanes, width, sidewalk…
const BUILDINGS = 'data/buildings.geojson'; // footprints with height or building:levels, roof:shape
const TREES = 'data/trees.geojson';         // points with a height (m) and a species

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const w = await world(canvas, {
  // sky(): the real sun and moon for the place and time; they light the world and cast its shadows
  body: earth({ imagery: [imagery.esri()], terrain: [terrain.mapzen()], sky: sky({ clouds: false }) }),
  view: { lon: 145.1215, lat: -37.9235, zoom: 17.8, tilt: 58, bearing: 30 },
  time: zonedTime('2026-01-15T16:00', 'Australia/Melbourne'),
  timeZone: 'Australia/Melbourne',
  render: { shadows: true },
  // the levels it is looked at: world › country › region › city › district › street › building › room
  observation: { levels: 'default' },
});

const near = { level: { from: 'district' } } as const;   // present from the district level in
w.add(
  roads({ id: 'roads', data: data.geojson(ROADS, { attribution: '© OpenStreetMap contributors' }), tooltip: (d) => String(d.props.name ?? 'road') }),
  buildings({ id: 'buildings', data: data.geojson(BUILDINGS), roofs: true, windows: { lit: 0.4 }, when: near,
    tooltip: (d) => `${d.props.building ?? 'building'} · ${d.props['height (m)']} m` }),
  vegetation({ id: 'trees', data: data.geojson(TREES), height: (d) => Number(d.props.height), species: (d) => String(d.props.species), when: near }),
);
// each change of the level (by the orbit, or by the app: w.setLevel('street'))
w.on('level', (e) => console.log(`level ${e.from} → ${e.to}`));
```

### fleet

A moving fleet from a log: half an hour of 24 buses (a CSV of samples: vehicle, time, place, battery) as one set of moving things on a light map. Each bus is drawn as a bus near the camera and a dot farther out, coloured by its battery, its wheels rolling by the distance it travelled, with a fading trail and a battery gauge over it; the log plays on the world's clock, looping.

```ts
import { drive, earth, entities, history, imagery, parseCSV, replay, terrain, world } from 'aslnut';
import { cars } from 'aslnut/modules/presets/vehicles';

// your log: one row per vehicle per sample (vehicle, time as ISO text, lon, lat, charge 0..1)
const LOG = 'data/trips.csv';

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const w = await world(canvas, {
  body: earth({ imagery: [imagery.esri({ layer: 'light' })], terrain: [terrain.mapzen()] }),
  view: { lon: 145.1215, lat: -37.9235, zoom: 16.8, tilt: 50, bearing: 0 },
});

// the log: each vehicle's samples, its battery a value carried with every sample (a byte: 0..1 in 255 steps), and the
// metres it has travelled (kept for the wheels)
const log = history.log({ values: { charge: { type: 'u8', domain: [0, 1] } }, travel: true });
const rows = parseCSV(await (await fetch(LOG)).text());
log.appendMany(rows.map((r) => ({ id: String(r.vehicle), t: String(r.time), lon: Number(r.lon), lat: Number(r.lat), values: { charge: Number(r.charge) } })));

w.add(entities({
  id: 'fleet', drive: drive.data(log),
  shape: cars.make({ type: 'bus' }),                         // near the camera; a dot farther out
  joints: { wheel: { value: 'travel' } },                     // every wheel (a joint of the shape) rolls by its bus's travel
  color: { value: 'charge', ramp: 'rdylgn', domain: [0, 1] }, // read from the samples at the world's time
  size: 8, outline: { color: '#ffffff', width: 1.5 },
  trail: { seconds: 90, width: 3 },
  // a bar over each with its per cent (by default only where the bus shape is drawn: `within` metres of the camera here)
  gauge: { value: 'charge', domain: [0, 1], label: true, within: 2000 },
  tooltip: (d) => `${d.id} · battery ${Math.round((d.state?.values.charge ?? 0) * 100)} %`,
}));

// the log's half hour on the world's clock: 10 times faster, looping
replay(w, { log, speed: 10, loop: true, play: true });
```

### analysis

An analysis view: the world muted to a dark blue-grey, districts coloured by a rate from one colour scale (quantile classes from the whole data) with their names inside the same layer, a legend that follows the data, a tooltip; the rows come from a query that runs again when the year changes, so the slider recolours the map (the shapes stay, only the changed colours ease).

```ts
import { data, earth, imagery, layer, legend, scale, terrain, theme, world } from 'aslnut';

// your data: the districts' shapes, and an API giving a row per district for a year ({ code, rate })
const DISTRICTS = 'data/districts.geojson';
const statsFor = async (year: number) => (await fetch(`data/stats-${year}.json`)).json();

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const w = await world(canvas, {
  body: earth({ imagery: [imagery.esri({ layer: 'light' })], terrain: [terrain.mapzen()] }),
  view: { lon: 145.1215, lat: -37.9235, zoom: 13.2, tilt: 25, bearing: 0 },
  theme: theme.dark(), // the world muted; elements marked `subject: true` keep their colours
});

// a knob of your own: the year (a slider, a timeline or an assistant sets it with w.set('stats.year', 2021))
w.param('stats.year', { type: 'number', range: [2019, 2025], default: 2025 }, () => {});

// the rows for the year: asked again whenever the year changes; joined to the shapes by their code
const districts = data.geojson(DISTRICTS, { id: 'code' });
const stats = data.query((s) => statsFor(Number(s.world.params['stats.year'])), { deps: (s) => s.world.params['stats.year'], id: 'code' });

// one statement: the districts coloured by their rate, with their names (the classes read from every district, again
// only when the rows change: never by the view)
w.add(layer({
  id: 'rate', label: 'Rate per 1,000', subject: true, data: districts.join(stats, { on: 'code' }),
  area: { color: scale.quantile((d) => Number(d.props.rate), { n: 5, range: 'viridis' }), opacity: 0.85, outline: { color: '#ffffff88', width: 1 }, restyle: 0.4 },
  labels: { text: (d) => String(d.props.name), size: 11, color: '#f1f5f9' },
  hover: { color: '#ffffff', mix: 0.3 }, tooltip: (d) => `${d.props.name}\n${d.props.rate} per 1,000`,
}));
legend(w, { for: 'rate', title: 'Rate per 1,000' });

// the year slider: setting the param runs the query again, and the map recolours
const slider = Object.assign(document.createElement('input'), { type: 'range', min: '2019', max: '2025', step: '1', value: '2025' });
Object.assign(slider.style, { position: 'fixed', right: '12px', bottom: '28px', zIndex: '10', width: '160px' });
slider.oninput = () => w.set('stats.year', Number(slider.value));
document.body.append(slider);
```

### own-kind

Your own design for a kind: a cottage that carries the house kind's traits (a roof, an entry at its front, parking outside, a service point), checked at every param's ends and placed on plots from data; and a model from a file made a house with its anchors (shapes.import), checked the same way. What uses a house reads only these traits.

```ts
import { color, data, earth, entities, imagery, int, kinds, num, roofFaces, shape, shapes, terrain, traits, world, type V3 } from 'aslnut';

// your data: plots (points with a heading: the way the front faces, degrees from north; a width; levels), a model
const PLOTS = 'data/plots.geojson';
const MODEL = 'models/house.glb'; // a glTF house; its front faces +z

// the design: a box of `levels` floors under a gable roof, a door at its front (+z), the house's anchors
const cottage = shape({
  id: 'cottage', kind: kinds.house,
  params: { width: num(6, 16, 9), depth: num(6, 14, 8), levels: int(1, 3, 1), floor: num(2.7, 3.4, 3), wall: color('#ece6da'), roofing: color('#8a5a44') },
  build: (b, p) => {
    const H = p.levels * p.floor, front = p.depth / 2, up = (pts: V3[]) => pts.map(([x, y, z]) => [x, y + H, z] as V3);
    // the walls as a group named 'walls': the kind measures the footprint from them (whatever else stands beside)
    b.group('walls', (b) => b.solid('box', { size: [p.width, H, p.depth], at: [0, H / 2, 0], color: p.wall }));
    // the roof as a group named 'roof': the kind measures its surface and tilt from it
    const roof = roofFaces('gable', p.width + 0.6, p.depth + 0.6, { pitch: 30 });
    b.group('roof', (b) => b.mesh(up(roof.slopes), { color: p.roofing }));
    b.mesh(up(roof.ends), { color: p.wall });
    b.solid('box', { size: [1, 2.1, 0.12], at: [0, 1.05, front + 0.06], color: '#5a3f2b' });
    // the house's traits: an entry at the front on the ground, parking outside the walls, a service point (a charger)
    b.anchor('entry-1', [0, 0, front + 0.8], { kind: 'entry', heading: 180 });
    b.anchor('parking-1', [p.width / 2 + 1.8, 0, front + 3], { kind: 'parking', heading: 180 });
    b.anchor('service-1', [p.width / 2 + 0.3, 0, front - 1], { kind: 'service' });
  },
});
// every param's ends and choices built and checked against the house kind (each trait missing or misplaced said once)
const checked = cottage.check({ kind: 'house' });
if (!checked.ok) throw new Error(`cottage: ${checked.problems.join('; ')}`);

// a model from a file, made a house: its anchors from its bounds (metres in its frame: its foot at 0, its front +z)
const model = await shapes.import(MODEL, {
  kind: 'house', length: 10, paint: false, params: { levels: 1 },
  anchors: (m) => ({
    'entry-1': { at: [0, 0, m.bounds[1][2] + 0.8], kind: 'entry', heading: 180 },
    'parking-1': { at: [m.bounds[1][0] + 2, 0, m.bounds[1][2] + 3], kind: 'parking', heading: 180 },
    'service-1': { at: [m.bounds[1][0] + 0.3, 0, 0], kind: 'service' },
  }),
});
const modelCheck = kinds.house.check(model);
if (!modelCheck.ok) throw new Error(`model: ${modelCheck.problems.join('; ')}`);

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const w = await world(canvas, {
  body: earth({ imagery: [imagery.esri()], terrain: [terrain.mapzen()] }),
  view: { lon: 145.1212, lat: -37.9236, zoom: 19.2, tilt: 55, bearing: 0 },
});
w.add(
  // a cottage on each plot, its params from the plot's data, turned to face its street
  entities({ id: 'cottages', shape: cottage, data: data.geojson(PLOTS),
    params: (d) => ({ width: Number(d.props.width), levels: Number(d.props.levels) }), heading: (d) => Number(d.props.heading) }),
  // the model house, placed as it is at two points
  entities({ id: 'models', shape: model, heading: () => 180, data: [
    { id: 'm1', props: {}, geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [145.1210, -37.9232] } },
    { id: 'm2', props: {}, geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [145.1214, -37.9232] } },
  ] }),
);

// the traits as anything that uses a house reads them (any design of a house answers the same)
const t = traits(cottage.make({ levels: 2 }), 'house'), r = t.roof as { surface: number; tilt: number };
const note = Object.assign(document.createElement('div'), { textContent: `cottage: a house · roof ${r.surface.toFixed(0)} m² at ${r.tilt.toFixed(0)}° · ${(t.parking as unknown[]).length} parking · ${(t.entries as unknown[]).length} entry` });
Object.assign(note.style, { position: 'fixed', left: '8px', bottom: '28px', zIndex: '10', background: 'rgba(12,16,24,.82)', padding: '6px 9px', borderRadius: '8px' });
document.body.append(note);
```

### own-thing

Your own thing: a watermill built from the builder's verbs, with three levels (the whole, a simpler one, its own far symbol), a wheel that turns by a joint driven by a rate, smoke from its chimney (copies over time, looping on the chip), and 240 mills that all look different with no build of their own: each clone is a record (its walls' and roof's colours, its size, its heading, its wheel's speed). One mill's wheel stops with one write.

```ts
import { earth, entities, imagery, num, roofFaces, shape, terrain, world, type V3 } from 'aslnut';

// the design, in metres in its own frame: its foot at y 0, its front +z
const mill = shape({
  id: 'mill',
  // params change its geometry (each distinct set is one build, cached); what only changes a look varies per clone
  params: { width: num(6, 12, 8), depth: num(6, 10, 7), wheel: num(2, 3.5, 2.8) },
  build: (b, p) => {
    const H = 5, front = p.depth / 2, up = (pts: V3[]) => pts.map(([x, y, z]) => [x, y + H, z] as V3);
    // the walls take each clone's colour (tint: true); the roof is a group: each clone can give it a colour of its own
    b.solid('box', { size: [p.width, H, p.depth], at: [0, H / 2, 0], color: '#e8e2d4', tint: true });
    const roof = roofFaces('gable', p.width + 0.6, p.depth + 0.6, { pitch: 35 });
    b.group('roof', (b) => b.mesh(up(roof.slopes), { color: '#7a4a36' }));
    b.mesh(up(roof.ends), { color: '#e8e2d4', tint: true });
    b.solid('box', { size: [1.2, 2.2, 0.1], at: [0, 1.1, front + 0.05], color: '#4a3524', detail: 1 }); // the door: whole and simple only
    // the chimney, and smoke from its top: copies over time (24 near, 8 at the simple level, none far)
    const top: V3 = [p.width / 4, H + 4.5, -p.depth / 4];
    b.solid('box', { size: [0.8, 4.5, 0.8], at: [top[0], H + 2.25, top[2]], color: '#8d877d' });
    b.frame({ at: top }, (b) => b.copy((b) => b.mesh([[-0.4, 0, 0], [0.4, 0, 0], [0, 0.7, 0]], { color: '#efefec' }),
      { emit: { count: [24, 8, 0], life: 4, rise: 12, spread: 2, grow: 2.5, fade: [0.7, 0], drift: [3, 1] } }));
    // the wheel on its side: a part that can turn round x at its hub (nothing turns it until the layer gives a driver);
    // eight paddles, copied round the hub, show it turning
    const hub: V3 = [p.width / 2 + 0.5, p.wheel, 0];
    b.part('wheel', (b) => {
      b.solid('cylinder', { radius: p.wheel * 0.8, size: 0.3, axis: 'x', at: hub, color: '#5b4632' });
      b.copy((b) => b.solid('box', { size: [0.6, 0.9, 0.12], at: [hub[0], hub[1] + p.wheel - 0.45, hub[2]], color: '#6b5640' }), { repeat: 8, turn: 45, axis: 'x', at: hub });
    }, { pivot: hub, joint: { kind: 'hinge', axis: 'x' } });
  },
  simple: true,                                                                         // level 1: the same build, fewer sides, no whole-only pieces
  far: (b, p) => b.solid('box', { size: [p.width, 7, p.depth], at: [0, 3.5, 0], color: '#e8e2d4', tint: true }), // level 2: its own symbol
  size: { min: 4 },                                                                     // never less than 4 CSS px across
});

// your data: the mills (points); here 240 made in code on a spiral round a place (about 440 m across)
const AT: [number, number] = [145.1215, -37.9235];
const mills = Array.from({ length: 240 }, (_, i) => {
  const r = 14 * Math.sqrt(i + 1), a = i * 2.39996, x = r * Math.cos(a), y = r * Math.sin(a);
  return { id: `m${i}`, props: { n: i, rpm: 2 + (i % 6) }, geometry: { type: 'Point' as const, coordinates: [AT[0] + x / (111320 * Math.cos((AT[1] * Math.PI) / 180)), AT[1] + y / 110574] as [number, number] } };
});
const WALLS = ['#e8e2d4', '#d9c9a8', '#c9d3d9', '#e3d0c4'], ROOFS = ['#7a4a36', '#4f5a62', '#8a6a3a'];
const n = (d: { props: Record<string, unknown> }) => Number(d.props.n);

const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas')!;
const w = await world(canvas, {
  body: earth({ imagery: [imagery.esri()], terrain: [terrain.mapzen()] }),
  view: { lon: AT[0], lat: AT[1] - 0.0002, zoom: 19.4, tilt: 64, bearing: 20 },
});

const valley = entities({
  id: 'mills', shape: mill, data: mills,
  params: (d) => ({ width: 6 + (n(d) % 3) * 2 }),                         // three widths: three builds for 240 clones
  variation: { seed: (d) => String(d.id), color: 0.06, scale: 0.12 },       // a seeded spread round each colour and size
  tint: (d) => WALLS[n(d) % 4]!,                                          // its walls' colour
  tints: { roof: (d) => ROOFS[(n(d) >> 2) % 3] },                          // its roof's colour
  heading: (d) => (n(d) * 47) % 360,
  joints: { wheel: (d) => ({ rate: Number(d.props.rpm), unit: 'rpm' }) }, // the chip turns each wheel from the clock
  pixels: { full: 90, simple: 20, margin: 0.2 },                           // each clone's level by its size on screen (CSS px)
});
w.add(valley);
valley.joint('m0', 'wheel', { rate: 0 });                                  // one write: the first mill's wheel stops
```

## Kinds

What every design of a kind carries: a shape says its kind (`shape({ kind: kinds.office, build })`), a model is given one (`shapes.import(url, { kind, anchors })`). Anchors are in the shape's frame: metres, its foot at y 0, its front +z; 'ground' is at y 0, 'front' in its front half, 'outside' beyond the walls' footprint, 'up' above the ground. The footprint is the box of the shape's group named 'walls' when it has one (`b.group('walls', …)`), else of all that stands over 0.3 m: draw the building only, and place what stands at an anchor (a charger, a car) as its own entity, or name the walls, or a post in the car park puts the bays inside the footprint. `shape.check({ kind })` builds the shape at its defaults and at every param's ends (each min and max) and every choice: the traits must hold at all of them (enough bays at the smallest width). Your own kind: `kind({ name, traits })`.

- house (a home: one household, a few cars): `kinds.house`
  - footprint: measured: its footprint; the box of its walls
  - front: measured: its front; the side to its street: +z
  - levels: the param 'levels' (guessed from a model); its floors
  - floor: the param 'floor' (guessed from a model); a floor's height, m
  - roof: measured: its roof; its kind, surface and tilt
  - entries: anchors of kind 'entry', at least 1, ground + front; where one walks in, from its front
  - parking: anchors of kind 'parking', at least 1, ground + outside; where a car stands
  - service: anchors of kind 'service', at least 1, ground; a charger or a meter: on a wall or a post
  - occupants: each thing's data 'occupants' (default 3); who lives there
- office (a workplace: many doors, a car park): `kinds.office`
  - footprint: measured: its footprint; the box of its walls
  - front: measured: its front; the side to its street: +z
  - levels: the param 'levels' (guessed from a model); its floors
  - floor: the param 'floor' (guessed from a model); a floor's height, m
  - roof: measured: its roof; its kind, surface and tilt
  - entries: anchors of kind 'entry', at least 2, ground + front; its doors, at its front
  - parking: anchors of kind 'parking', at least 4, ground + outside; its car park's bays
  - service: anchors of kind 'service', at least 1, ground; chargers at its bays
  - workers: each thing's data 'workers' (default 40); who works there
- charger (a place to charge electric vehicles: a station or a wall charger): `kinds.charger`
  - bays: anchors of kind 'parking', at least 1, ground; where a car stands to charge
  - ports: the param 'ports'; its ports
  - power: the param 'power'; kW
  - connector: the param 'connector'; its plug
  - lights: anchors of kind 'light', one per bays, up; each bay's status light
- vehicle (a road vehicle): `kinds.vehicle`
  - wheels: parts named 'wheel…', at least 2; its wheels (they spin, the front ones steer)
  - doors: parts named 'door…', at least 1; its doors (they open)
  - seats: anchors of kind 'seat', at least 1; where one sits
  - entries: anchors of kind 'entry', at least 1, ground + outside; where one gets in

## API index

Every part of aslnut that exists (built: in the package and tested on WebGPU and WebGL2; partly: some of it, said what), by its id in the one tree, with its signature, params (type = default), returns and an example. Parts not there yet are named only: do not use them.

### core.space (docs/reference/core/space.md)

- core.space.bodies [partly]: `body(options)` · `w.bodies`
  params: `id: string` · `radius?: number` · `ellipsoid?: [a, b]` · `plane?: { size }` · `gravity?: number = 9.81` · `rotation?: { period, axis }` · `surface?: Surface`
  returns: `Body`
  e.g. `body({ id: 'ceres', radius: 469_700 })`
- core.space.precision [built]: camera-relative positions
  returns: centimetres at street level, no jitter
  e.g. (automatic)
- core.space.ground.ground [partly]: `w.ground.at(lon, lat)` · `w.ground.normal(lon, lat)` · `on: 'ground'` · `w.standAt(lon, lat, near?)` (where a thing stands: the top of what is drawn there, a road, a kerb, a footpath, a deck, the level nearest `near`; the ground where nothing is drawn; layers that draw such surfaces give `levelsAt(lon, lat, out)`)
  params: `lon, lat: number` · `near?: number` (true m)
  returns: `metres` · `[x, y, z]`
  e.g. `const h = await w.ground.at(107.61, -6.9)`
- core.space.regions.tree [built]: `regions.tree({ levels, sources, parentOf? })` · `await tree.load(loader)` · `tree.at(lon, lat, level?)` · `tree.get(level, id)` · `tree.parent(r)` · `tree.children(r)` · `tree.path(r)` · `tree.level(name)`
  params: `levels: string[]` (top first) · `sources: Record<level, Source>` · `parentOf?: Record<level, f => id>` (default: the parent its middle lies in)
  returns: `RegionTree` · `Region { id, level, name, props, parent }`
  e.g. `tree.at(107.61, -6.9, 'district')`
- core.space.regions.rollup [built]: `tree.rollup(rows, opts)` · `groups(options)` (things rolled up into groups per level, with values over time)
  params: `rows: Source` · `on: string` (the rows' region id) · `to: level` · `from?: level` · `sum?: string[]` · `mean?: string[]` · `count?: boolean` · `fn?: (rows, region) => props`; groups: `of: id | Element | Source | array` (a set's moving things: in a group while inside it; features) · `by: { regions: Source | Feature[], name? } | { cells: m } | d => key | { [level]: by }` · `values?: { [name]: { count: true } | { sum | mean | min | max: Channel } | { of: Channel, fn: values => number } } = { n: count }` · `log?` · `show?: { levels: string[] }` (the groups there, the members at the others) · `mark?: (g: GroupsSource, level) => Element` (default a label each)
  returns: `Rows` at the target level (live: changes with the rows) · `Groups` (an element; a level's `GroupsSource`: a feature a group (its area, its cell, its members' middle) and its `log`: each group a thing, its values over time)
  e.g. `tree.rollup(crime, { on: 'suburb', to: 'lga', sum: ['count'] })` · `groups({ of: 'places', by: { regions: suburbs }, values: { n: { count: true } }, show: { levels: ['city', 'district'] }, mark: (g) => cards({ of: g, rows: [{ label: 'places', value: 'n' }] }) })`

not there yet (planned, proposed or open; do not use):
  core.space.frames.inertial, core.space.frames.body-fixed, core.space.frames.local, core.space.frames.object,
  core.space.frames.re-rooting, core.space.units, core.space.cells, core.space.ground.shells, core.space.ground.volumes,
  core.space.regions.pack, core.space.observer.light-time, core.space.observer.aberration, core.space.observer.doppler,
  core.space.observer.ship-time

### core.time (docs/reference/core/time.md)

- core.time.clock [built]: `w.time` · `w.setTime(t, { rate })` · `w.setTimeRate(n)` · `w.timeRate`
  params: `t: Date | 'now'` · `rate?: number` (seconds per second; with a date the default is 0: the time held; with 'now' 1) · `zone?: string = local`
  returns: `s.time = { t, date, hour, day, year, rate, paused, zone }`
  e.g. `w.setTime(new Date('2026-06-21T15:00+07:00'), { rate: 600 })`
- core.time.step [built]: `w.step(ms)` · `world(canvas, { clock: 'manual' })`
  params: `ms` (the world advanced by that much and one frame drawn)
  returns: `this`
  e.g. `for (let i = 0; i < 600; i++) w.step(1000 / 30)`
- core.time.zones [built]: `s.time.local` · `world(canvas, { timeZone })` · `w.setTimeZone(zone)` · `w.timeZone` · `zoneLookups.nearest(opts)` · `zoneLookups.fixed(name)` · `zonedTime(wall, zone)`
  params: `timeZone?: IANA name | 'auto' | (lon, lat) => name | null` (auto: the place's under the camera, asked again every 25 km; unset: solar time) · `nearest: { near?: km = 1500 }`
  returns: local time for the place: `{ year, month, day, hour, minute, weekday, zone, offset }`
  e.g. `world(canvas, { timeZone: 'auto' })` · `when: s => s.time.local.hour >= 18`

not there yet (planned, proposed or open; do not use):
  core.time.calendars, core.time.scales, core.time.ranges, core.time.deep

### core.data (docs/reference/core/data.md)

- core.data.sources.tiles.xyz [built]: `raster.xyz(url, opts?)` · `imagery.custom({ url })`
  params: `url: string` (`{z}/{x}/{y}`, `{-y}`) · `minZoom?: int = 0` · `maxZoom?: int = 18` · `attribution?: string` · `terms?: Partial<Terms>` · `where?: BBox`
  returns: `RasterSource`
  e.g. `raster.xyz('https://…/{z}/{x}/{y}.png')`
- core.data.sources.tiles.wms [built]: `raster.wms(url, opts)` · `raster.wms.capabilities(url, opts?)` · `raster.wms.legend(url, layer, opts?)` · `raster.wms.info(url, { layers, lon, lat, zoom? }, opts?)` · `raster.view({ url: (box, width, height) => string })`
  params: `layers: string` · `styles?: string` · `format?: string = 'image/png'` · `version?: string = '1.3.0'` · `transparent?: boolean = true` · `params?: Record<string, string>` · `single?: boolean = false` (one picture of the view in CRS:84 instead of EPSG:3857 tiles: drawn on the chip as a mark, stacked among vector layers, its opacity a uniform; asked again when the view reaches new ground or comes 1.6× closer, never while it moves, after a failure only after 2 s doubling to a minute) · `maxSize?: px = 2048` · `scale?: = 1` (picture px per CSS px at the centre) · `headers?` · `fetch?` · `proxy?: string | (url) => string`
  returns: `RasterSource` (tiles, painted into the ground) · `ViewSource` (`single`; its `legend` (GetLegendGraphic) and `wms: { url, layers, version }`) · capabilities: `{ version, title, layers: [{ name, title, crs, bbox, queryable, legend, styles }], formats, infoFormats }` (1.3.0, else 1.1.1) · info: the features there as GeoJSON, each with its `layer`
  e.g. `raster({ id: 'zones', source: raster.wms(url, { layers: 'ns:plan_zone', single: true }), opacity: 0.5 })`
- core.data.sources.tiles.pmtiles [built]: `data.pmtiles(url, opts?)`
  params: `url: string` (read by byte ranges) · `layer?: string | string[]` · `id?: string` (a prop that is the id) · `zoom?: number | 'view' = 'view'` · `maxTiles?: int = 64` · `linger?: ms = 0` (tiles the view left kept among the features while it moves and that long after) · `attribution?`
  returns: `Source` (MVT tiles for the view; pieces of one id joined; cut edges marked)
  e.g. `data.pmtiles('/tiles/suburbs.pmtiles', { layer: 'suburbs', id: 'code' })`
- core.data.sources.tiles.mvt [built]: `data.mvt(url, opts)`
  params: `url: string` (`{z}/{x}/{y}`, `{-y}` for TMS rows) · `layer?: string | string[]` · `id?` · `minZoom?: int = 0` · `maxZoom?: int = 14` · `bounds?: BBox` · `zoom?: number | 'view' = 'view'` · `maxTiles?: int = 64` · `linger?: ms = 0` (tiles the view left kept among the features while it moves and that long after) · `attribution?`
  returns: `Source` (vector tiles for the view; pieces of one id joined)
  e.g. `data.mvt('…/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf', { layer: 'roads' })`
- core.data.sources.files.geojson [built]: `data.geojson(url | object, opts?)`
  params: `id?: string | (f, i) => id` (default: the GeoJSON `id`, else the index) · `attribution?: string`
  returns: `Source`
  e.g. `data.geojson('/plants.geojson', { id: 'gid' })`
- core.data.sources.files.csv [built]: `data.csv(url | text, opts?)`
  params: `lon?: string = 'lon'` · `lat?: string = 'lat'` · `id?: string | fn` · `delimiter?: string` (found by itself) · `numbers?: boolean = true`
  returns: `Source` (rows; points where they have coordinates)
  e.g. `data.csv('/stations.csv', { id: 'code' })`
- core.data.sources.services.wfs [built]: `data.wfs(url, opts)` · `data.wfs.capabilities(url, opts?)` · `data.wfs.describe(url, typeName, opts?)`
  params: `typeName: string` (with its prefix) · `extent?: BBox` (the box it loads, once; unset: the whole layer when it is small (at most `most` features, counted first), else an error that says to give one) · `tiles?: boolean = false` (true: the view's tiles instead, asked as the view moves; they only add features by id, never replace or reload them; a scale over it needs its domain) · `most?: int = 20000` (the whole layer loaded when it has at most this many) · `orExtent?: BBox` (no extent and the whole layer too big: this box instead) · `version?: '2.0.0' | '1.1.0' | 'auto' = 'auto'` (2.0.0, then 1.1.0 when refused) · `filter?: string | { cql } | { fes }` (the extent's box added to it; FES as 2.0.0 writes it, asked of 1.1.0 as `ogc:`) · `geometryName?: string` (a filter's: default DescribeFeatureType's) · `crs?: string` (default EPSG:4326 when offered, else web Mercator (turned back to degrees), else GDA94 / GDA2020 read as degrees; projected only: E-DATA-001) · `format?: string = 'application/json'` · `id?: IdRule` (default the service's feature id) · `pageSize?: = 1000` (count / startIndex; maxFeatures in 1.1.0) · with `tiles`: `gridOffset?: = 1` · `minGrid?: = 10` · `maxGrid?: = 15` · `maxFeatures?: = 5000` (a tile's most) · `maxTiles?: = 24` · `bounds?: BBox` · `headers?` · `fetch?` · `proxy?: string | (url) => string` (a service without CORS) · `attribution?`
  returns: `WFS` (a Source loaded once over its extent, paged, its features handed on together when every page is in; with `tiles`: the screen's own tiles, nearest first, each asked once, features only added by id; `info: { version, crs, requests, bytes, tiles, truncated, features, ms }`) · capabilities: `{ version, title, layers: [{ name, title, crs, bbox }]` …
  e.g. `area({ id: 'suburbs', data: data.wfs('https://…/geoserver/wfs', { typeName: 'ns:locality_polygon', extent: [144.9, -38.0, 145.3, -37.8] }) })`
- core.data.sources.services.stream [built]: `data.stream(url | { url?, connect? })`
  params: `connect?: emit => stop` (your simulation, poller or library) · `parse?: data => message` · `retry?: seconds = 2` (doubling to 30) · `id?` · messages: rows (upserted) or `{ set?, upsert?, patch?, remove? }`
  returns: `Stream` (a live Source; `close()`)
  e.g. `data.stream('wss://…/fleet')` · `data.stream({ connect: emit => sim.on('tick', emit) })`
- core.data.sources.custom [built]: `data.custom({ load, id? })`
  params: `load: (ctx) => Promise<Feature[] | Row[] | GeoJSON>` (`ctx.loader` for cached fetches) · `attribution?`
  returns: `Source`
  e.g. `data.custom({ load: async () => (await fetch('/api/plants')).json() })`
- core.data.loading.loader [built]: `loader(opts)` · `w.loader.get(url, opts)`
  params: `mode?: 'live' | 'record' | 'replay' | 'offline' = 'live'` · `kind?: 'tile' | 'json' | 'binary'` · `priority?: number` · `scope?: string`
  returns: `Promise<Response-like>`
  e.g. `world(canvas, { loader: { mode: 'offline' } })`
- core.data.loading.stores [built]: tiers: memory → packs → browser cache → network
  params: `memoryMB?: number = 256` · `cache?: boolean = true`
  e.g. `loader: { memoryMB: 128 }`
- core.data.loading.packs [built]: `data.pack(url)` · `w.loader.record(name)` · `pack.save()`
  params: `url: string` (a pack or a manifest)
  returns: `Pack`
  e.g. `loader: { packs: [data.pack('/packs/bandung')] }`
- core.data.loading.readiness [built]: `w.ready.plan(views)` · `w.ready.coverage(views)` · `w.ready.ensure(views, opts)` · `w.ready.rehearse(views)`
  params: `views: (View | name)[]` · coverage `scope?` · ensure `{ scope?, concurrency?, onProgress? }` · rehearse `{ timeout? }`
  returns: plan `{ needed: url[] }` · coverage `{ needed, have, missing, fraction }` (kept in packs and the scope's store) · ensure what was fetched and kept (where the terms allow keeping) · rehearse per view `{ settled, ms, frames, pending, missing }` (the camera put back)
  e.g. `await w.ready.ensure(['city'])`
- core.data.loading.tiles [built]: tiled sources load the view's tiles by themselves (loading is a cache: invisible; features only added by id while the view moves, the far ones let go only off screen): `data.pmtiles(url)` · `data.mvt(template)` · `data.geojson(template)` (a URL with `{z}`)
  params: `zoom?: number | 'view' = 'view'` (the view's level within the source's, or a fixed one: the whole extent) · `maxTiles?: int = 64`
  returns: the features of the view's tiles, pieces of one id joined, shown when every wanted tile is in
  e.g. `data.geojson('/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.geojson', { maxZoom: 14 })`
- core.data.loading.chunks.format [partly]: `header · layers[positions, normals, colours, far-count] · solids`
  params: `quantize?: { xz: 'auto' | number, y: number = .02 }` · `layers?: string[] = ['solid', 'mark', 'water', 'buildings']`
  returns: 14 bytes per corner
  what is there: baked road tiles, v2: JSON per 500 m tile of typed pieces with heights, `{ v, ix, iz, size, infos, pieces }`: areas (an outline and holes, each point's height), edges (a line with heights, ground and the kerb's inward offset), strips, walls, boxes; the binary format planned
  e.g. `quantize: { y: .01 }`
- core.data.features.features [built]: `Feature { id, props, geometry, cuts? }`
  params: `id` stable across loads (from the data, a prop, or your function; a repeat kept apart) · `geometry` GeoJSON's types in lon / lat · `cuts` (tile edges, not outlined)
  returns: `source.features()` · `source.get(id)`
  e.g. `suburbs.get('vic-3168').props.name`
- core.data.features.rows [built]: `data.rows(array?, opts?)` · `rows.set(array)` · `rows.rows()`
  params: `array: object[]` · `id?: string | fn = 'id'` · `lon? / lat?` (rows with coordinates are points)
  returns: `Rows` (a Source; geometry only where it has coordinates)
  e.g. `const crime = data.rows([])`
- core.data.query.join [built]: `shapes.join(rows, opts)`
  params: `on: string | f => key` (the shapes' prop, or `'id'`) · `rowsOn?: string | f => key` (when named differently)
  returns: `Joined` (a Source; rows that change recolour, shapes stay; `matched`)
  e.g. `suburbs.join(crime, { on: 'suburb_code' })`
- core.data.query.query [built]: `data.query(fn, opts?)` · `q.refresh()`
  params: `fn: (s) => rows | GeoJSON | Promise` · `deps?: s => any` (runs again when it changes; default once; the time or the state, never the view: data is never changed by looking) · `when?: When` · `every?: seconds` · `debounce?: ms = 150` · `map?: answer => rows`
  returns: `Query` (Rows; the latest answer wins; `answeredFor`)
  e.g. `data.query(s => api.crime(s.world.params['q.year']), { deps: s => s.world.params['q.year'] })`
- core.data.live.set [built]: `rows.set(array)`
  params: `array: Row[] | GeoJSON`
  returns: replaces all; shapes rebuild only if shapes changed, else colours ease
  e.g. `crime.set(await fetchRows())`
- core.data.live.upsert [built]: `rows.upsert(items)`
  params: `items: Row[]` (by id)
  returns: — (a new id plays its reveal)
  e.g. `fleet.upsert([{ id: 'B1', lon, lat }])`
- core.data.live.patch [built]: `rows.patch(id, props)`
  params: `id` · `props: Partial`
  e.g. `fleet.patch('B1', { soc: .58 })`
- core.data.live.remove [built]: `rows.remove(...ids)`
  params: `ids: (string | number)[]`
  e.g. `fleet.remove('B1')`
- core.data.history.log [built]: `history.log(options)` · `log.append(id, t, lon, lat, values?, props?)` · `log.appendMany(rows)` (a row's `alt`) · `history.fromColumns({ ids, count, start?, t, lon, lat | lonlat, alt?, values?, props? }, options?)` · `log.toBytes({ things? })` · `history.fromBytes(bytes, { keep?, travel?, altitude? })` · `history.smallest({ box, from, to })`
  params: `values?: Record<name, 'u8' | 'f32' | { type, domain, step? }>` (`step: true`: a state, a code, a flag: held from each sample to the next, never mixed through the values between: read, derived, on the chip, kept in a saved log) · `place?: { type: 'u16' | 'f32' = 'f32', box? }` · `time?: { type: 'u16' | 'f32' = 'f32', epoch?, step?: s = .1 }` · `keep?: samples = 512` (a live thing's ring; `Infinity`: all) · `url?` (a saved log, loaded through the world's loader) · `travel?: boolean` (it keeps each sample's metres along its thing's track since its first: a value 'travel', kept as samples come, for a recorded track and once loaded; what a wheel rolls by) · `altitude?: 'ground' | 'sea' | { over, type: 'u8' | 'f32' = 'f32', domain?, value = 'alt' }` (each sample's height: metres over what it stands on or over the sea, a value of its own (`values.alt`, a row's `alt`, a point's third coordinate); `log.at(…).alt`; `log.altMax`; kept in a saved log)
  returns: `Log`: things (ids, props), each one's samples in typed columns of the smallest type (16-bit places in a box, 16-bit times in steps, a byte a value), `watch(fn)` (the slots each change touched) · relations over time: `history.relations(rows, { of?, to?, from?, until?, kind? })` · `history.relations.fromLog(log, { value, to: (v` …
  e.g. `history.log({ url: '/data/fleet.hist' })` · `log.append('bus-12', Date.now(), 145.12, -37.92, { charge: .8 })`
- core.data.history.state-at [built]: `log.stateAt(t, ids?)` · `log.at(id, t)`
  params: `t: number | Date | string` · `ids?: (string | number)[]`
  returns: `StateAt[]`: `{ id, lon, lat, heading, speed, values, props, outside }` (between two samples; the heading along its path, held while it stands)
  e.g. `log.stateAt('2026-10-15T08:15+11:00')`
- core.data.history.replay [built]: `replay(w, opts)`
  params: `from?, to?: Date | string | ms` (default the log's span) · `speed?: number = 1` · `loop?: boolean = false` · `play?: boolean = false` · `log?`
  returns: `Playback`: `play()` · `pause()` · `toggle()` · `setSpeed(x)` · `seek(t, { share? })` · `on(fn)` · `playing` · `progress`
  e.g. `const p = replay(w, { log, speed: 60, loop: true }); p.play(); p.seek(.5, { share: true })`
- core.data.scenarios.base [built]: `w.scenario.use('base')` · `w.scenario.current` · `w.scenario.list()`
  returns: the world as it is (everything a scenario changed, put back)
  e.g. `w.scenario.use('base')`
- core.data.scenarios.variant [built]: `w.scenario(name, opts)` · `w.scenario.use(name)`
  params: `base?: string = 'base'` (its changes under this one's) · `set?: Record<sourceId | layerId, Source | Feature[]>` · `params?: Record<key, value>` · `rules?: Record<fieldId, Rule | { rule, params }>` · `label?`
  returns: `Scenario`
  e.g. `w.scenario('more-trees', { set: { trees: planned } })`
- core.data.scenarios.diff [built]: `w.scenario.diff(a, b)`
  params: `a, b: string`
  returns: `Promise<{ added, removed, changed, params, rules }>` (features as { source, id }; params as { key, a, b }; rules as { field, a, b })
  e.g. `await w.scenario.diff('base', 'more-trees')`
- core.data.scenarios.compare [built]: `w.scenario.compare(a, b, opts)` · `w.scenario.compare(null)` · `w.scenario.setSplit(at)`
  params: `view?: 'split' | 'swipe' | 'difference' = 'split'` · `at?: 0..1 = .5`
  e.g. `w.scenario.compare('base', 'v2', { view: 'swipe' })`
- core.data.rights.terms [built]: `terms: Terms` on every source
  params: `{ show, prefetch, keep, export }`
  e.g. `imagery.custom({ terms: { keep: false } })`
- core.data.rights.capabilities.show [built]: `terms.show`
  params: `boolean | { maxZoom?, where? } = true`
  e.g. `show: { maxZoom: 18 }`
- core.data.rights.capabilities.prefetch [built]: `terms.prefetch`
  params: `boolean | { maxZoom? } = true`
  e.g. `prefetch: { maxZoom: 16 }`
- core.data.rights.capabilities.keep [built]: `terms.keep`
  params: `boolean | { days? } = false`
  returns: whether packs may store it
  e.g. `keep: { days: 30 }`
- core.data.rights.capabilities.export [built]: `terms.export`
  params: `boolean | { watermark? } = false`
  returns: whether captures may include it
  e.g. `export: { watermark: true }`
- core.data.rights.attribution [built]: `w.attribution()` · on screen: `world(canvas, { attribution })` · in captures: `w.frame({ attribution: true })`
  params: `attribution?: false | { position?: 'bottom-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'top-right' | 'top-left' = 'bottom-right', className?, format?: credits => string }` (false: the app shows them itself)
  returns: `string[]` (for what is on screen now)
  e.g. `w.attribution()`

not there yet (planned, proposed or open; do not use):
  core.data.sources.tiles.cog, core.data.loading.chunks.manifest, core.data.loading.chunks.logic-pack,

### core.observation (docs/reference/core/observation.md)

- core.observation.observers.orbit.views [built]: `w.go(view)` · `w.addView(name, view)` · `w.fly(to, opts)` · `w.fit(target, opts)` · `w.viewToFit(target, opts)` · `w.setProjection(p, seconds?)` · `world(canvas, { frame })` · `w.camera.tiltLimit` · `w.camera.clear`
  params: `view: { lon, lat, dist? | zoom?, tilt?: degrees = 0, bearing?: degrees = 0 }` (both dist and zoom when they agree: `w.camera.view` written back as it is, camera keys' views too) · `tilt`: up to 88° with the eye at street level or below (30 m over the ground under the centre), 80° from 300 m up, eased between (`tiltLimit: { low: 88, high: 80, street: 30, above: 300 }`; a zoom out from the street takes the tilt back to the map's) · `clear?: metres | false = 1` (the eye kept over the ground and what is stood on under it, whatever moves it: a hand, a flight, a move; false: a view from under the ground) · `target: [w, s, e, n] | Feature | Feature[]` · `padding?: number = .08` · `maxZoom?` · `p: 'auto' | 'globe' | 'flat'` (eased over `seconds = 1.2`: the globe opens into the map) · `frame?: 'auto' | 'height' = 'auto'` ('auto': a portrait screen sees as much across as a landscape one, so a zoom shows the same place whole on a phone)
  returns: `Promise<void>` (fly, fit) · a view (viewToFit: the box whole on this canvas, any shape)
  e.g. `await w.fit(suburb, { padding: .1, tilt: 30 }); w.setProjection('flat')`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.keys [built]: `camera.keys(list)`
  params: `list: { at: seconds, view: View, ease?: Ease, path?: Path }[]`
  returns: `Playback`
  e.g. `camera.keys([{ at: 0, view: a }, { at: 6, view: b, ease: 'cinematic' }])`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.paths [built]: `path`
  params: `'direct' | 'arc' | 'around' = 'direct'` · `around?: { centre, turns }` (between two views; built) · or a `Path` from the kinds below
  e.g. `path: 'arc'`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.paths.line [partly]: `paths.line(from, to)`
  params: `from, to: View | Point`
  returns: `Path` (straight)
  what is there: : today as a key's `path: 'direct'`; `paths.line` planned
  e.g. `paths.line(here, there)`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.paths.circle [partly]: `paths.circle(centre, opts)`
  params: `centre: Point | Entity` · `radius: metres` · `turns?: number = 1` · `up?: metres` · `tilt?: degrees`
  returns: `Path` (a circle or part of one)
  what is there: : today as a key's `path: 'around'` with `turns`; `paths.circle` planned
  e.g. `paths.circle(tower, { radius: 300, turns: .25 })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.aim [partly]: `aim: Aim` (a move's first argument, or `move({ aim })`)
  params: one of the kinds below
  what is there: look-at; along-path, heading, framing planned
  e.g. `moves.chase(lookAt(plane, { raise: .2 }))`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.aim.look-at [built]: `lookAt(target, opts?)` · `track(log, id, opts?)`
  params: `target: [lon, lat, h?]` (h: metres over the sea) `| { lon, lat, up?, heading? }` (up: metres over the ground) `| point name | track(log, id, { up })` (a thing on a log, wherever the world's time puts it; `up`: metres or your function of where it is) `| (timeMs) => …` · `lead?: seconds` (look ahead of where it goes) · `raise?: share of half the screen = 0` (where it sits: up from the middle)
  returns: `Aim`
  e.g. `lookAt(track(planeLog, 'plane', { up: altAt }))`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.speed.easing [built]: `ease`
  params: `'smooth' | 'cinematic' | 'glide' | 'snap' | 'anticipate' | 'overshoot' | 'cubic-bezier(a,b,c,d)' = 'smooth'`
  e.g. `ease: 'glide'`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.moves [partly]: `w.play(move, opts)` · `w.playing` · `move({ aim, keys, damping, over, seconds })` (your own, from the same parts)
  params: `opts: { seconds?, ease? }` (no seconds: it holds its first key until stopped) · a move is four parts: the path (`keys: { at: 0..1, rig: { dist, tilt, bearing | turn, raise } | 'now', ease? }[]`: the rig round what it looks at, `turn` from the thing's heading, 'now' where the camera is when it starts), the aim (`lookAt`), the damping (follow's springs), the speed (each key's ease) · `over?: metres | false` (the eye kept over what stands near it, eased: up quickly, down slowly)
  returns: `Promise<void>` (it ends at its seconds, on a new move, a flight, a jump, or a person's hands moving the camera)
  what is there: one engine for every preset; a move after another on the same thing carries its springs on; what a move of a second or more will see loads ahead; `.with`, `.then`, `seek` planned
  e.g. `await w.play(moves.crane(car, { up: 400, swing: 30 }), { seconds: 6 })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.dolly [built]: `moves.dolly(target, opts)`
  params: `in? | out?: metres` (along the line of sight, from where the camera is) or `to?: metres` · `ease?` · `damping?`
  returns: `Move`
  e.g. `moves.dolly(fountain, { in: 50 })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.crane [built]: `moves.crane(target, opts)`
  params: `up?: metres = 30` · `back?: metres = 0` (farther along the ground) · `swing?: degrees = 0` (round it) · or `to?: rig` · from where the camera is (a crane up from a chase's own eye)
  returns: `Move`
  e.g. `moves.crane(car, { to: { dist: 1400, tilt: 52, turn: 30 } })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.arc [built]: `moves.arc(target, opts)`
  params: `degrees?: number = 90` (clockwise seen from above; negative the other way) · `dist?`, `tilt?` (kept unless given) · `from?: rig` (default where the camera is)
  returns: `Move` (part of an orbit round it)
  e.g. `moves.arc(place, { degrees: 110 })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.track [built]: `moves.track(target, opts?)`
  params: `side?: metres = 8` (to its left; negative its right) · `up?: metres = 2` · `to?: rig` (a track that falls back behind it) · `raise?`
  returns: `Move` (alongside a moving thing, looking across at it)
  e.g. `moves.track(plane, { side: 77, up: 14, raise: .15 })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.chase [built]: `moves.chase(target, opts?)`
  params: `behind?: metres = 12` · `up?: metres = 4` · `turn?: degrees = 0` (round it from straight behind) · `to?: rig` (a chase that drifts round) · `over?: metres = 4` (over what stands near the eye) · `damping?` (default: the follow's)
  returns: `Move`
  e.g. `moves.chase(track(log, 'car'), { behind: 42, up: 16 })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.reveal [built]: `moves.reveal(target, opts?)`
  params: `from?: 'below' | 'behind' | 'side' = 'behind'` (from close in: low and near, rising; near from behind, pulling back and up; near from its side, coming round) · `dist?: metres = 40` · `to?: rig` (default 55° from straight down) · `ease?: 'cinematic'`
  returns: `Move`
  e.g. `moves.reveal(fountain, { from: 'below', dist: 30 })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.follow [built]: `w.follow(target, opts?)` · `w.follow(null)` · `w.isFollowing` · `followEntity(w, entity, opts)`
  params: `target: point name | [lon, lat, h?] | { lon, lat, up?, heading? } | track(log, id) | (timeMs) => …` (a vehicle, a player, a storm; a thing in the air stays at the middle of the screen) · `heading?: true | degrees` (the view turns with it) · `dist?: metres` (the eye kept that far) · `damping?: { place, aim, dist, heading: { halfLife?: s | stiffness?: 1/s², deadZone?, maxSpeed?, lead?, from?: 'motion' | 'thing' }, snap?: metres | false }` (a critically damped spring per channel, exact on the world's clock: the same camera at any frame rate; a dead zone, a look ahead (default: the spring's own lag, so a thing going steadily is followed with none), a top speed; the heading the short way round, from the way it goes; a jump farther than `snap` (default twice the distance) cuts) · `smooth?: ms` (the old knob: the place's half-life that lags as much) · for entities: `offset?: [right, up, behind] = [0, 3, -8]` · `lag?` · `look?` · `yaw?`, `pitch?` · `blocked?`
  returns: `this` · a stop function
  e.g. `w.follow(track(log, 'bus-12'), { heading: true, damping: { heading: { halfLife: 1 } } })`
- core.observation.observers.orbit.acrobatic [built]: automatic: every gesture, flight, key and follow
  returns: each frame only the picture's uniforms change (the view's matrices): nothing is loaded, rebuilt, recoloured or faded because the eye moved; a level changes only through the binding and its gates
  e.g. (a pinch from street to region and back in 2 s: 0 loads, 0 restyles, 0 fades)
- core.observation.levels.ladder [built]: `world(canvas, { observation: { levels } })` · `w.observe(options | null)` · `w.levels`
  params: `levels?: 'default' | (string | { name, from })[]` · `'default'`: world (from zoom −∞) › country (3.5) › region (6.5) › city (9.5) › district (12.5) › street (14.5) › building (17) › room (19); a list of names cuts the default (each keeps its default edge); `{ name, from }`: your own rungs, coarse to fine (`from`: the zoom it starts at) · unset: no levels (a GIS map), nothing gated, nothing measured
  returns: the ladder: `{ name, from }[]`, coarse first
  e.g. `observation: { levels: ['city', 'district', 'street', 'building'] }`
- core.observation.levels.level [built]: `w.level` · `w.setLevel(name)` · `w.on('level', f)` · `s.observation` · `w.observation` (the ladder, the gates and what they did: `{ level, by, waiting, swapping, counts: { changes, swaps, released, waitedMs } }`, for an observation panel)
  params: `name: string` (a rung of the ladder; an unknown one is an error that lists them)
  returns: `w.level`: the name now (null: no levels) · the event `{ from, to, by: 'orbit' | 'app' }` · `s.observation: { level, index, levels, by }`
  e.g. `w.setLevel('street')` · `when: s => s.observation.level === 'room'`
- core.observation.levels.binding [built]: `observation: { bind }`
  params: `bind?: 'orbit' | false | (s) => string = 'orbit'` ('orbit': the orbit's zoom drives the level through the gates; false: the app alone sets it; your function: another observer's rule, asked as the state changes)
  returns: — (the app's `setLevel` holds until the orbit crosses the next edge past the margin)
  e.g. `observation: { levels: 'default', bind: false }`
- core.observation.gates.margin [built]: `observation: { margin }`
  params: `margin?: number = 0.3` (zoom levels past an edge before the level changes: hysteresis; back across needs the same margin the other way)
  e.g. `observation: { margin: 0.5 }`
- core.observation.gates.dwell [built]: `observation: { dwell }`
  params: `dwell?: seconds = 0.5` (how long the orbit stays past the margin before the level changes: a debounce; a burst over an edge and back changes nothing) · `ahead?: number = 1` (zoom levels before an edge where the next level's data loads quietly)
  e.g. `observation: { dwell: 1 }`
- core.observation.gates.keep [built]: `observation: { keep }`
  params: `keep?: { levels?: int = 2, seconds?: number = 60 }` (the last levels' data and built shapes kept: going back is instant; past it, freed)
  returns: — (a level change swaps once: the new level's things shown together when ready, the old ones until then)
  e.g. `observation: { keep: { levels: 3, seconds: 120 } }`
- core.observation.presence [built]: `when: (s) => boolean | number` or a shorthand, on every element and every feature (`feature: { when }`)
  params: `s: State` · shorthand `{ level?: name | name[] | { from?, to? }, hour?: [a, b], month?: [a, b], year?: [a, b], api?, quality?, role?, toggle? }` (`level`: one rung, a set of rungs, or a range on the ladder; with no ladder set, `level` turns the default one on) · or `boolean = true` · no `when`: always shown (a GIS layer: no gate)
  returns: `boolean | 0..1` (fraction = partly shown); a change by level plays once, at the level change (the gates); `when: { zoom }` is an error with its fix (the camera never decides presence: use `level`; a function of `s.view` still works if you insist)
  e.g. `when: { level: { from: 'district' }, hour: [18, 6] }` · `when: s => s.user.toggles.crime`

not there yet (planned, proposed or open; do not use):
  core.observation.observers.orbit.paths.bezier, core.observation.observers.orbit.paths.spline,

  core.observation.observers.orbit.aim.heading, core.observation.observers.orbit.aim.framing,
  core.observation.observers.orbit.lens, core.observation.observers.orbit.lens.fov,
  core.observation.observers.orbit.lens.focus, core.observation.observers.orbit.lens.depth-of-field,
  core.observation.observers.orbit.speed, core.observation.observers.orbit.speed.ease,
  core.observation.observers.orbit.speed.constant, core.observation.observers.orbit.speed.hold,
  core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.pan, core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.tilt,
  core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.roll, core.observation.observers.orbit.moves.truck,
